audits.title: Evaluating Adherence to Rapid Tranquilization Protocols in Psychiatric Emergencies: An Audit of a Tertiary Care Facility in Pakistan
audits.standard: Rapid tranquillisation protocol for psychiatric emergencies (stepwise de-escalation, oral then IM medication, post-administration monitoring)

cycle1.result: Only 60% adhered to recommended protocol steps; 68% bypassed oral medication or de-escalation; vital sign monitoring after administration not recorded in 30%.

audits.other_findings: 12% needed a second injection, with the interval undocumented in 15% of these; medication unavailability affected 8% of aggressive cases, and ECG before haloperidol was omitted.
audits.citation: Gul N, Nizami A. Evaluating Adherence to Rapid Tranquilization Protocols in Psychiatric Emergencies: An Audit of a Tertiary Care Facility in Pakistan. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S233-S234. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.571.

audits.title: Audit of Non-Pharmacological and Rapid Tranquilisation Practices in Managing Distress Among Older Adults: A Comparative Study in Inverness Hospitals
audits.standard: Local protocols for managing distress in older adults (non-pharmacological approaches and rapid tranquilisation)
audits.setting: Old Age Psychiatric Ward, Acute Medical Unit and Geriatric Ward, hospitals in Inverness

cycle1.result: Nurses consistently used non-pharmacological de-escalation before RT, in line with the local protocol; physical restraint only used where there was risk, by trained staff; junior doctors, especially in AMU, had limited understanding of the RT protocol.

audits.other_findings: Further education and training on the RT protocol for junior doctors was recommended.
audits.citation: Kumar P, Wild A, Howells F, Kumar T, Williams P. Audit of Non-Pharmacological and Rapid Tranquilisation Practices in Managing Distress Among Older Adults: A Comparative Study in Inverness Hospitals. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S244-S245. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.594.

audits.title: Clinical Audit of Rapid Tranquilisation in Mental Health Services for Older People (MHSOP)
audits.setting: Two older people's mental health inpatient wards, Auckland Park Hospital

cycle1.result: Choice and dose within recommendations in all cases. Baseline NEWS observations in all; full post-RT observations at correct intervals in 33% (refusals documented). De-escalation documented and post-RT debrief in 100%; medication review post-RT in 66%.

audits.other_findings: 33% had a raised NEWS after RT, resolving spontaneously; no documented side effects.
audits.citation: Hern D, Salim T, Oduma M, Langford W. Clinical Audit of Rapid Tranquilisation in Mental Health Services for Older People (MHSOP). BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S252-S252. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.610.

audits.title: Re-Evaluating Rapid Tranquillisation Practices in Elderly Patients (over 65 Years of Age) at a General Hospital: A Follow-Up Audit
audits.standard: Local mental health trust rapid tranquillisation guidance
audits.setting: Six wards (three geriatric, two medical, one surgical), district general hospital

cycle1.result: 13/297 (4.3%) received RT; indication documented in 50%; maximum frequency not indicated; no psychiatric liaison or dementia team involvement evident; post-RT monitoring not evident.

cycle2.result: 9/172 (5.2%) received RT; indication documented in 88.8%; maximum frequency indicated in 55.5%; almost 100% documentation of RT administration; liaison or dementia team involvement around 33%; post-sedation monitoring still not evident.

audits.other_findings: PRN and intramuscular remained most common. A new RT policy with teaching and training has since been approved, with re-audit planned in 6–12 months.
audits.citation: Singh H, Wrench H, Jenkinson J. Re-Evaluating Rapid Tranquillisation Practices in Elderly Patients (over 65 Years of Age) at a General Hospital: A Follow-Up Audit. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S263-S264. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.634.

audits.title: Audit of Rapid Tranquillisation Prescribing and Monitoring Practices at Rohallion Medium and Low Secure Forensic Psychiatry Unit, Murray Royal Hospital, NHS Tayside
audits.standard: Local and national guidance: 100% documented plan for oral and IM as-required medication; 100% offered oral before IM; 100% side-effect monitoring within 1 hour of rapid tranquillisation
audits.setting: Rohallion Clinic medium and low secure forensic psychiatry unit, Murray Royal Hospital, NHS Tayside

cycle1.result: 38 (81%) had as-required medicines prescribed; 24 (63%) of these had a documented plan; reasons for IM medication and side-effect monitoring documented 25.42% of the time. Standards 1, 2 and 3 not met.

audits.intervention: Action plan: work with clinical team and pharmacist to improve documentation, and add headers to online assessment templates. Re-audit planned.
audits.other_findings: Lorazepam was most often prescribed, in line with local guidance; dosing frequency (mostly 4-hourly) was compliant.
audits.citation: Unni A, Maior O, Bate J. Audit of Rapid Tranquillisation Prescribing and Monitoring Practices at Rohallion Medium and Low Secure Forensic Psychiatry Unit, Murray Royal Hospital, NHS Tayside. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S286-S286. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10693.

audits.title: Audit and Re-Audit of Pre-Rapid Tranquillisation (Pre-RT) Workup and Documentation in an Inpatient Psychiatry Ward at Allied Hospital II, Faisalabad.
audits.standard: Pre-RT standards from NICE guidance, Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines and BAP/NAPICU consensus
audits.setting: Inpatient psychiatry ward, Allied Hospital II, Faisalabad

cycle1.result: De-escalation documented 71%; clear indication 83%; pre-RT workup 47%; baseline observations 85%; capacity/consent 90%; cardiac/QT risk 85% (haloperidol); reassessment before repeat dosing 42%; airway risk 78% (benzodiazepines); contraindications/interactions 66%.

audits.intervention: Structured pre-RT checklist and staff education.

cycle2.result: De-escalation 92%; clear indication 96%; pre-RT workup 85%; reassessment before repeat dosing 92%; airway risk 92%; contraindications 85%; other domains met or exceeded standards.

audits.other_findings: Medication details were documented in 100% at baseline.
audits.citation: Fatima S, Dogar I, Fatima D, Sajid P, Yazdani H. Audit and Re-Audit of Pre-Rapid Tranquillisation (Pre-RT) Workup and Documentation in an Inpatient Psychiatry Ward at Allied Hospital II, Faisalabad. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S271-S272. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11571.

audits.title: Rapid Tranquillisation in Scunthorpe Acute Psychiatric Inpatient Service: A Re-Audit Highlighting Gender Differences, Clinical Trends, and NICE Compliance
audits.standard: NICE NG10 (2015); traffic-light compliance green ≥80%, orange 60–79%, red <60%
audits.setting: Mulberry Ward, acute adult psychiatric inpatient ward, Scunthorpe

cycle1.result: 37 RT incidents in 17 patients; seclusion used in 30%; compliance figures not given.

cycle2.result: 79 RT incidents in 10 patients; seclusion fell to 5%; NICE compliance remained excellent for risk assessment, patient rights and documentation, but post-RT monitoring, debriefing, medication review and incident reporting remained below standard.

audits.other_findings: Advance directives were absent in both audits. RT frequency among women rose from 2.2 to 10.5 incidents per patient, and lorazepam became the main agent (43% to 69.6%).
audits.citation: Shahpesandy H, Baruah A, Freeman K, Bisma S, Tuxworth D. Rapid Tranquillisation in Scunthorpe Acute Psychiatric Inpatient Service: A Re-Audit Highlighting Gender Differences, Clinical Trends, and NICE Compliance. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S283-S283. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11742.
